source.title: Trimer Covers in the Triangular Grid: Twenty Mostly Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Consider the finite triangular-grid regions called (a,b)-benzels, tiled by five trihex prototiles: a right-pointing stone, a left-pointing stone, and three bone orientations. Let T003(a,b) count tilings that allow no stones and all three bone orientations. For k >= 2, what exact formula governs T003(k(3k-1)/2, k(3k+1)/2)? More weakly, is there a recurrence or other counting method that is substantially more efficient than brute-force enumeration for these bone-only benzels?

evidence.quote: Figure 4: The five prototiles: the right stone, the left stone, the vertical bone, the rising bone, and the falling bone.
Prior to the conference, I was able to show that if an (a, b)-benzel can be tiled by bones alone, then we must have a = k(3k - 1)/2 and b = k(3k + 1)/2 (or vice versa) for some k >= 2.

Problem 1: Find an exact formula for T003 (k(3k - 1)/2, k(3k + 1)/2). Of course, even short of an exact formula, any method of determining the number of tilings that is more efficient than brute-force enumeration (e.g., a recurrence relation) would be of interest.

accepted.question_text: Let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T012(3n, 3n) = 2^n n! for every n >= 1?
accepted.context_brief: left stones two bones diagonal formula

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 2: Is it true that T012 (3n, 3n) = 2^n n! for n >= 1?
Comment: Colin Defant, Rupert Li, Benjamin Young and I worked on problem 2 during the conference and later succeeded in solving Problems 2 and 3; see [3].

accepted.question_text: Let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T012(3n+1, 3n+2) = 2^n n! for every n >= 1?
accepted.context_brief: left stones two bones offset formula

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 3: Is it true that T012 (3n + 1, 3n + 2) = 2^n n! for n >= 1?
Comment: Colin Defant, Rupert Li, Benjamin Young and I worked on problem 2 during the conference and later succeeded in solving Problems 2 and 3; see [3].

accepted.question_text: Let T013(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel is negative or zero, must a type-013 tiling exist?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
When a and b are such that the Conway-Lagarias invariant is negative or zero, the entries in the table are observed to be positive, though I see no reason for concluding that they are.
Problem 4: Is it true that when the Conway-Lagarias invariant associated with the (a, b)-benzel is negative or zero, tilings of type 013 exist?

accepted.question_text: Let T102(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which right stones are allowed, left stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that for all k >= 0 and n >= 1, except (k,n) = (0,1), one has T102(n+3k, 2n+3k-1) = product_{i=1}^k ((2i)! (2i+2n-2)!)/((i+n-1)! (i+n+k-1)!)?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 5: Is it true that T102 (n + 3k, 2n + 3k - 1) = product_{i=1}^k ((2i)!(2i + 2n - 2)!)/((i + n - 1)!(i + n + k - 1)!) for k >= 0 and n >= 1 (except (k, n) = (0, 1))?
This formula and the a, b symmetry relation together provide a conjectural enumeration of tilings of type 102 of the (a, b)-benzel for all a, b satisfying a + b equiv 2 (mod 3).

accepted.question_text: Let T103(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which right stones are allowed, left stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T103(n, 2n-3) = (3n+3)(3n-7)!/((n-5)! (2n-1)!) for every n >= 5, with the same formula also yielding 0 for n = 3 and n = 4 if one formally interprets 1/(-1)! and 1/(-2)! as 0?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.

Problem 6: Is is true that T103 (n, 2n - 3) = (3n + 3)(3n - 7)!/(n - 5)!(2n - 1)! for n >= 5? (The formula also works for n = 3 and n = 4 if one treats 1/(-1)! and 1/(-2)! as 0.) Equality has been verified for 5 <= n <= 16.

accepted.question_text: Let T103(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which right stones are allowed, left stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel is positive or zero, must a type-103 tiling exist?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.

When the Conway-Lagarias invariant of a benzel is strictly negative, the benzel cannot be tiled by bones and right-pointing stones; the corresponding entries in the table must be zero. On the other hand, when a and b are such that the Conway-Lagarias invariant is positive or zero, the entries in the table are observed to be positive, though I see no reason for concluding that they are.
Problem 7: Is it true that when the Conway-Lagarias invariant associated with the (a, b)-benzel is positive or zero, tilings of type 103 exist?

accepted.question_text: Let T(n) = T112(3n, 3n), where T112(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that for every n >= 1 the second quotient T(n) T(n+2) / T(n+1)^2 equals 256(2n+3)^2(4n+1)(4n+3)^2(4n+5) / (27(3n+1)(3n+2)^2(3n+4)^2(3n+5))?

We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.

Problem 8: With T (n) denoting T112 (3n, 3n), is it true that the second quotient T (n)T (n + 2)/T (n + 1)^2 is equal to 256(2n + 3)^2 (4n + 1)(4n + 3)^2 (4n + 5) / (27(3n + 1)(3n + 2)^2 (3n + 4)^2 (3n + 5)) for all n >= 1?

accepted.question_text: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. What formula governs T112(3n+1, 3n+1) for n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
With T (n) = T112 (3n + 1, 3n + 1) with n >= 1, it appears that T (n) has no prime factor greater than or equal to 4n.
Problem 9: Find a formula governing T112 (3n + 1, 3n + 1). See OEIS entry A364481.

Is it true that for every n >= 1 the quotient T(n) T(n+3) / (T(n+1) T(n+2)) equals 65536(2n+3)(2n+5)^2(2n+7)(4n+3)(4n+5)^2(4n+7)^2(4n+9)^2(4n+11) / (729(3n+2)(3n+4)^3(3n+5)^2(3n+7)^2(3n+8)^3(3n+10))?

We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.

accepted.question_text: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. What formula governs T112(3n-1, 3n) for n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
With T (n) = T112 (3n - 1, 3n) with n >= 1, it appears that T (n) has no prime factor greater than or equal to 4n.
Problem 11: Find a formula governing T112 (3n - 1, 3n). See OEIS entry A364483.

accepted.question_text: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T112(n+2, 2n+1) equals the nth large Schroder number for every n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 12: Is it true that T112 (n + 2, 2n + 1) is the "nth large Schroder number" for all n >= 1? Equality has been verified for 1 <= n <= 15.

accepted.question_text: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T112(n+2, 2n) equals the number of royal paths in a lattice of order n for every n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 13: Is it true that T112 (n + 2, 2n) is the number of "royal paths in a lattice of order n" for all n >= 1? Equality has been verified for 1 <= n <= 15.

accepted.question_text: Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever a+b is congruent to 1 modulo 3, is it true that T113(a,b) = 1, so that the region has exactly one tiling?
accepted.context_brief: unique all-tiles tiling when a+b=1 mod 3

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.

Problem 14: Is it true that T113 = 1 when a+b is 1 (mod 3)? (Note that a + b equiv 1 is the situation in which the Conway-Lagarias invariant coincides with the area of the region being tiled, so that all the tiles must be right-pointing stones.)
Comment: This problem is resolved in the affirmative by Theorem 1.1 of [3].

accepted.question_text: Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-4), defined for n >= 5, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 15: Is T113 (n, 2n - 4) 2-adically continuous as a function of n >= 5?
The sequence appears to be constant mod 2, constant mod 4, 2-periodic mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16.

accepted.question_text: Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 16: Is T113 (n, 2n - 3) 2-adically continuous as a function of n >= 4?
The sequence appears to be constant mod 2, constant mod 4, 2-periodic mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16.

accepted.question_text: Let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-4; 3), defined for n >= 5, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

evidence.quote: Let Tijk (a, b; 3) denote the weighted sum of the i, j, k tilings of the (a, b)-benzel as defined near the end of section 1, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m.
Problem 17: Is T113 (n, 2n - 4; 3) 2-adically continuous as a function of n >= 5?
The sequence appears to be constant mod 2, constant mod 4, constant mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16.

accepted.question_text: Let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3; 3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

evidence.quote: Let Tijk (a, b; 3) denote the weighted sum of the i, j, k tilings of the (a, b)-benzel as defined near the end of section 1, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m.
Problem 18: Is T113 (n, 2n - 3; 3) 2-adically continuous as a function of n >= 4?
The sequence appears to be constant mod 2, constant mod 4, 2-periodic mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16.

accepted.question_text: For tilings of a finite simply-connected region in the hexagonal grid by stones and bones, there are two natural local 2-flip moves: one replaces two oppositely oriented stones by two bones, and the other replaces a stone-and-bone pair by a stone of the same orientation together with a bone of a different orientation. Can every such tiling be transformed into every other such tiling by a finite succession of these 2-flips?

evidence.quote: There are two natural kinds of "2-flips" that can turn one stones-and-bones tiling into another; the first trades two stones of opposite orientation for two bones, and the second trades a stone and a bone for a stone of the same orientation and a bone of a different orientation.
Problem 19: Can every tiling of a finite simply-connected region using stones and bones be mutated into every other such tiling by means of a
succession of 2-flips?

accepted.question_text: Let T_n be the triangular region of hexagonal cells with n cells on each side. When stones alone are used as tiles, Conway, Lagarias, and Thurston showed that T_n is tileable exactly for n congruent to 0, 2, 9, or 11 modulo 12. As n tends to infinity through those congruence classes, does the number of stone tilings of T_n converge 2-adically to 0?
accepted.context_brief: 2-adic limit for stone tilings of triangular regions

evidence.quote: Triangles of hexagonal cells, with n cells on each side ("T_n regions"). Those three authors showed that if one uses stones alone, T_n can be tiled by T_2's precisely when n is congruent to 0, 2, 9, or 11 (mod 12).
Problem 20: As n goes to infinity within the set of natural numbers congruent to 0, 2, 9, or 11 (mod 12), does the number of tiling of T_n by stones converge 2-adically to 0?
